# Brief 03: Cost reduction

Audience: Pinnacle Retail Group executive board.
Decision: approve a $43M run-rate cost programme with $21M of one-time spend.
Format: 9 slides, density balanced. Start with a cover and end with next steps.
Data: data.csv holds spend and savings by cost category used on slides 3 and 5.

## Facts

F1: Addressable operating cost is $412M a year: store labour 168, logistics 74, marketing 52, IT 41, real estate 38, indirect procurement 39 (USD million).
F2: Savings potential by category (USD million): store labour 14.0, logistics 9.5, marketing 6.2, IT 5.3, real estate 2.5, indirect procurement 5.5; total 43.0.
F3: Operating cost is 24.8% of sales at Pinnacle; the peer median is 22.9% and the best peer is 21.6%.
F4: Peer operating cost as % of sales: Peer A 21.6, Peer B 22.4, Peer C 23.4, Peer D 24.1.
F5: Sales are $1.66B, so $43M of savings is 2.6% of sales.
F6: One-time cost to achieve is $21M; payback is about 6 months once run-rate is reached.
F7: Savings phasing (USD million, run-rate in year): FY26 12, FY27 31, FY28 43.
F8: Store labour: scheduling to demand cuts idle hours by 9%; 41% of stores run the same roster all week.
F9: Logistics: 38% of trucks leave under 70% full; consolidating routes saves $9.5M.
F10: Marketing: 27% of promotional spend has no measured return.
F11: Risk: store labour savings above $14M put service levels at risk; customer satisfaction must stay above 82.
